pages.title: The complete heritage model
pages.subtitle: All 16 persistent content entities and all 22 declared foreign keys. Detailed attributes follow on the detailed diagrams.
notes: Each R-number identifies a physical foreign key; the complete register appears on the relationship register below.
The four operational tables are separate from this content model and are shown on the operations diagram.

pages.title: Places, monuments and primary classification
pages.subtitle: State / UT -> heritage site -> monument. Each monument has one primary building type and may have alternate names.
notes: All columns are shown. PK = primary key; FK = foreign-key participant; UQ = single-column uniqueness; ? = nullable.
Site state is a natural-key reference to states.name. Map fields are approximate site reference points.
Narratives, construction ranges and individual coordinates remain properties of buildings.

pages.title: Materials, styles and architectural elements
pages.subtitle: Three many-to-many relationships, resolved through occurrence / junction tables.
notes: buildings is abbreviated here; its complete definition is on the catalogue diagram. All category and junction fields are shown.
UNIQUE(building_id, material_id), UNIQUE(building_id, style_id), UNIQUE(building_id, element_id).
Local usage_notes / descriptions belong to the monument-category pair, not to the shared category definition.

pages.title: Evidence, sources and assertion targets
pages.subtitle: A citation supports one monument, comes from one source, and may identify at most one specific occurrence.
notes: Sources and citations show all columns. Repeated monument/junction cards show only relevant keys.
CHECK(num_nonnulls(building_style_id, building_material_id, building_element_id) <= 1).
The three optional target FKs include building_id. This prevents evidence targeting another monument's occurrence.

pages.title: Photographs and monument anatomy
pages.subtitle: An image belongs to a monument. A hotspot connects a position on that image to a local architectural element.
notes: Images, hotspots and building_elements show all columns. buildings is abbreviated; see the catalogue diagram.
Hotspot -> image uses (building_id, storage_key); hotspot -> occurrence uses (building_id, element_id).
UNIQUE(building_id, storage_key, element_id); x/y are 0-100 percentages. Element-specific citation checks are application-level.
A partial unique index allows at most one cover image per building; publication prerequisites are application-level.

pages.title: A monument's life through sourced events
pages.subtitle: Construction, additions, alterations, restorations, changes of use and recognition are separately dated records.
notes: Sources and building_events show all columns. buildings repeats only identification and construction-period fields.
Event years are -4000..2100, excluding zero; year_from <= year_to. Negative years represent BCE.
Building year zero is also rejected. NULL construction dates remain unknown; no historical influence relationship is implied.

pages.title: Authentication and runtime bookkeeping
pages.subtitle: Four permanent operational tables. No foreign keys are declared between these tables and the content entities.
notes: Only column definitions are shown: no account, password-hash or session values are included.
The application stores administrator session identity inside sessions.sess JSON; this is not a declared relational FK.
schema_migrations records applied SQL files; seed_tasks prevents curated data from being reapplied over administrator edits.
published_building_summary is a SQL view over buildings, sites and building_types, not another stored table.

pages.title: DBMS Lab: temporary practice models
pages.subtitle: Disposable PostgreSQL TEMP tables created per exercise connection. None is a permanent catalogue entity.
notes: Constraint / transaction exercises use lab_sites, lab_buildings and lab_links. UNIQUE(building_id, material) prevents duplicate non-null associations.
Practice site_id and building_id FKs are nullable in the actual teaching setup; their optional cardinalities are shown accurately.
lab_scale is an unrelated 40,000-row synthetic table made with CREATE TABLE AS. No PK or FK is declared; a site_id index is added for measurement.
No relationship to permanent monuments exists. Closing the connection destroys these tables after each exercise.
